t: You're in Brompton Cemetery, laid out in 1839 and opened in 1840. Since 1852 it has been Crown property, the first London cemetery to be so, and it's managed by The Royal Parks. It's one of the Magnificent Seven. Emmeline Pankhurst, who organised the British suffragette movement, is buried here. So is Hertha Ayrton, the electrical engineer and suffragette who invented an anti-gas fan in the First World War. Also here are Dr John Snow, who traced a Soho cholera outbreak to a water pump, and the chemist William Crookes, inventor of the Crookes tube. Samuel Smiles, author of Self-Help, and the chess master Johannes Zukertort lie here as well.
